author: haiku
label: seeded-01-01
changes: Stated every design choice the brief left to the author (storage, Redis decision, session IDs, expiry check, cleanup, lockout mechanics, cookie lifetime, redirect code, storage-failure behavior). The draft named the tables but left these unstated.
Explained why Postgres is used instead of Redis and why it is sufficient.
Explained the two expiry limits (30-minute idle, 12-hour absolute) and how the database clock is used to check them.
Added the rule that failures are recorded for unknown emails too, so the 429 response does not reveal which accounts exist. Also added the dummy-hash step to keep response timing even.

Specified the exact status codes and messages: 401 with 'Invalid email or password' for bad credentials, 429 for lockout, 303 redirects. The draft's 'goes back to the login page with an error' was vague.

Expanded the Mermaid sequence diagram into labeled alt branches for locked, bad credentials, success, valid session, and missing or expired session, with logout. Removed semicolons and other characters that can break Mermaid message text.
Defined terms such as fail closed, bcrypt, SHA-256 and advisory lock in plain language so a reader outside the project can follow the design.
Added explicit fail-closed behavior for database errors on login, protected pages, logout and cleanup. The draft only said 'Handle DB errors'.
Added an open-boundaries section for the per-email lockout limit, its denial-of-service trade-off, and out-of-scope features.
Kept the original intent and format: a Mermaid sequenceDiagram with short notes before and after it, and the same four tables.
Added a short terms list (cookie, bcrypt, transaction, advisory lock, fail closed, 303 redirect) so a reader new to the stack can follow the design.

Expanded the Choices section to explain why each choice matters, for example why Redis is not used, what SHA-256 hashing protects against, what HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite each do, and what the advisory lock prevents. Stated each choice explicitly as the brief asked.
Split the Stored data and Lockout bullets into clearer sub-points and wrote out what each column means.

Rewrote the Sequence section intro and added notes below the diagram for the lock transaction, the lock-before-password order, the last_seen_at update, and logout behaviour, since those rules do not fit on the arrows.
Reworded diagram messages to plain phrasing and removed semicolons, which Mermaid can treat as line breaks. The sequence structure and all three flows are unchanged.
Added to the Rules at a glance that the 503 case keeps the cookie, and that locked attempts are not checked against the password, so the summary matches the detailed rules.
Did not add a rule for what happens if the last_seen_at update fails after a valid session check. The brief does not decide this, so the reviewer should decide it before build.
Defined the terms a newcomer needs: session, hash, row, primary key, and the HTTP status codes used. Added a plain explanation of what a session is and why the cookie holds only an ID.
Added a numbered 'Login, step by step' section that gives the order of checks in plain words before the diagram.
Split the 'Left to you' choices into named subsections (state location, session IDs, expiry checks, cleanup, lockout, storage failures) that each state the choice and its reason.
Clarified that the lock check, the password check and the failure insert are separate steps, and that only the lock check, failure count and insert share one transaction.

Added an open boundary that the original did not state: requests that passed the lock check before the fifth failure was recorded can still be checked against the password. This follows from the separate steps in the diagram.
Added an open boundary noting that the 429 lock message wording is not specified in the brief.
Kept the sequence diagram and its notes, with only minor label wording changes, such as 'none if unknown' in place of 'may be none'.
Kept all fixed requirements, the storage choices and the 503 behaviour unchanged.
